intended_object: One piece of a step function used to show that binary addition is in FP. It reads the encoded adder state `pair x (pair y (pair carry accRev))` and returns the carry-out word of a full adder, computed from the head bits of the two remaining operands and the current carry. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation of MachineBinaryAdd.lean.
explanation: This definition is internal machinery. It belongs to a hand-built bounded-iteration machine for binary addition. It works on a library-specific pairing encoding of the adder state as a `List Bool`, and it only exists so that `machineBinaryAddAdvanced` and `machineBinaryAddStep` can be assembled and shown to be in `Complexity.FP`. It has no standalone counterpart in the mathematical literature. The underlying notion, the carry-out of a full adder (the majority of a, b and c), is not what is being defined here. What is defined is that function composed with the library's projections out of the state encoding. As an implementation detail it is consistent with its docstring. The lemma `machineBinaryAddStep_pack` shows that, on well-formed states, the new carry is `(a && b) || (a && c) || (b && c)`, where a and b are the operand head bits (defaulting to false on an empty list) and c is the current carry. That is the correct full-adder carry. So nothing is wrong with it, but it is a technical device rather than a mathematical object.
